paper.title: On the Robustness and Provenance of the Gambler’s Fallacy

claims.claim: Experiment 1a probability-judgment posterior median effect size was -0.11, 95% CrI [-0.27, 0.05].
Experiment 2a at 60% ground truth had posterior median effect size -0.34, 95% CrI [-0.50, -0.18].
Experiment 3 had posterior median effect size -0.33, 95% CrI [-0.50, -0.17].
In Experiment 3, 7.33% of participants’ P(repeat) values were below 40%.
Experiment 1a one-sample Wilcoxon result was Z = -1.03, p = .304, r = .08.

findings.description: Experiment 1a posterior effect does not recur: script median -0.2164 (95% interval [-0.32790, -0.09971]) versus reported -0.11 [-0.27, 0.05].
findings.suggested_fix: Review the Experiment 1a analysis-to-report mapping and resolve the source of the discrepancy before describing this value as reproduced.

limitations: The script computes several tests without printing their statistics; those reported values cannot be checked without adding output code.
No robustness or scientific-conclusion assessment was conducted.
